vocabulary.meaning_en: to give someone the important facts about something
vocabulary.example: I need to brief the manager before the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a difficult situation
vocabulary.example: We were in a predicament when the flight was cancelled.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not going to happen any more
vocabulary.note_ar: في الأمريكية تُكتب canceled بحرف l واحد.
vocabulary.example: Our flight to London is cancelled.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to book again, often for a different time
vocabulary.example: They rebooked us on the next flight.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to deal with a problem or arrange something
vocabulary.example: Don't worry, I've sorted out a hotel.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to keep someone informed about what is happening
vocabulary.example: Please keep me in the picture about the order.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to tell someone the latest news regularly
vocabulary.example: I'll keep you informed about the delivery.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give someone the newest information; new information
vocabulary.example: Could you update me on the project?

vocabulary.meaning_en: to finish a deal successfully
vocabulary.example: We closed the deal yesterday.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to continue or start doing something that was planned
vocabulary.example: We need to proceed with the order quickly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very fast; with no delay
vocabulary.example: Please reply as quickly as possible.

vocabulary.meaning_en: willing to work hard to do something
vocabulary.note_ar: بعد committed to نستخدم الفعل مع ing.
vocabulary.note_en: After committed to, use the -ing form.
vocabulary.example: I'm committed to finishing on time.

vocabulary.meaning_en: at the correct time, not late
vocabulary.example: The order arrived on time.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a time when something happens later than planned
vocabulary.example: There is a delay because of the weather.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the battery has no power left
vocabulary.example: Can I use your phone? My battery has run out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to take and use something that belongs to someone else, and give it back
vocabulary.note_en: Borrow (you take) is the opposite of lend (you give).
vocabulary.example: Could I borrow your pen?

vocabulary.meaning_en: when your phone is no longer connected
vocabulary.example: I lost the signal in the lift.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to understand what someone means
vocabulary.example: I think he got the message.

vocabulary.meaning_en: when you have to begin your day very early
vocabulary.example: We've got an early start tomorrow.

vocabulary.meaning_en: being friendly and generous to guests
vocabulary.example: Thank you for your kind hospitality.

vocabulary.meaning_en: behaving in a correct and serious way at work
vocabulary.example: Let's keep things professional.

fine_lines.title: borrow vs lend
fine_lines.explanation_ar: borrow تعني أن تأخذ شيئًا من غيرك مؤقتًا، و lend تعني أن تعطي شيئًا لغيرك مؤقتًا. نقول: Could I borrow your phone? أو Could you lend me your phone?
fine_lines.explanation_en: Borrow means you take something for a short time. Lend means you give something for a short time. Could I borrow your phone? = Could you lend me your phone?

examples.sentence: Could I borrow your mobile phone, please?
Could you lend me your charger?

fine_lines.title: in the picture vs in the photo
fine_lines.explanation_ar: keep someone in the picture تعبير اصطلاحي يعني إبقاء الشخص على اطلاع، ولا علاقة له بالصور. أما in the photo فمعناها حرفي: داخل الصورة.
fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Keep someone in the picture' is an idiom meaning keep them informed; it has nothing to do with photos. 'In the photo' is literal.

examples.sentence: Please keep the boss in the picture.
Who is the man in the photo?

expressions.phrase: It's good news – I've closed the deal and the contract is signed.
expressions.meaning_ar: خبر جيد: أتممت الصفقة وتم توقيع العقد.
expressions.meaning_en: Telling your boss a deal is finished successfully.
expressions.example: It's good news – I've closed the deal and the contract is signed.

expressions.phrase: We need to proceed with the order as quickly as possible.
expressions.meaning_ar: علينا أن نمضي في تنفيذ الطلب بأسرع ما يمكن.
expressions.meaning_en: We must start the order without delay.
expressions.example: To keep the client happy, we need to proceed with the order as quickly as possible.

expressions.phrase: I'm committed to getting the order delivered on time… but I will need some help.
expressions.meaning_ar: أنا ملتزم بتسليم الطلب في موعده، لكنني سأحتاج إلى بعض المساعدة.
expressions.meaning_en: I will work hard to deliver on time, but I need help.
expressions.example: I'm committed to getting the report finished on time, but I will need some help.
Remember to keep your manager in the picture.

expressions.meaning_en: A way to start telling good news.
expressions.example: Hi Paul, it's Anna. I've got some good news!

expressions.phrase: Could I borrow your mobile phone, please?
expressions.meaning_ar: هل يمكنني استعارة هاتفك المحمول من فضلك؟
expressions.meaning_en: A polite request to use someone's phone.
expressions.example: Could I borrow your mobile phone, please? Mine is not working.

expressions.meaning_ar: أتساءل إن كان بإمكان توم أن...
expressions.meaning_en: A soft, polite way to ask for something.
expressions.example: I wonder if Tom could help me with the order.

expressions.meaning_en: My phone is no longer connected.
expressions.example: Sorry, I've lost the signal. I'll call you back.

grammar.title: committed to + verb-ing
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد committed to (وكذلك look forward to) يأتي الفعل مع ing، لأن to هنا حرف جر وليست جزءًا من المصدر: I'm committed to getting… وليس committed to get.
grammar.explanation_en: After 'committed to' the verb takes -ing, because 'to' here is a preposition (like 'look forward to'): I'm committed to getting… not 'committed to get'.
examples: I'm committed to getting the order delivered on time.
We are committed to helping our customers.
She is committed to improving her English.

grammar.title: Present perfect for news
grammar.explanation_ar: نستخدم المضارع التام (have/has + التصريف الثالث) لنقل خبر جديد حدث للتو ونتيجته مهمة الآن: I've closed the deal.
grammar.explanation_en: Use the present perfect (have/has + past participle) to give new news that matters now: I've closed the deal.
examples: They've rebooked us on the next flight.

grammar.title: Polite requests with Could I…? / I wonder if…
grammar.explanation_ar: لطلب مهذب نستخدم Could I + الفعل؟ للاستئذان، و I wonder if + جملة لطلب أكثر لطفًا وأقل مباشرة.
grammar.explanation_en: For polite requests use 'Could I + verb?' to ask permission, and 'I wonder if + clause' for an even softer request.
examples: Could I borrow your mobile phone, please?
I wonder if Tom could help me.
I wonder if you could call me back later.

questions.question: What does 'brief the manager' mean?
choices: give the manager the important facts
questions.explanation_ar: brief كفعل تعني إطلاع شخص على المعلومات المهمة.
questions.explanation_en: To brief means to give someone the important facts.

questions.question: 'Keep Paul in the picture' means…
questions.explanation_ar: keep someone in the picture تعني إبقاءه على اطلاع.

questions.question: Complete: 'I'm committed to ___ the order delivered on time.'
questions.explanation_ar: بعد committed to نستخدم الفعل مع ing.

questions.question: Complete: 'We need to ___ with the order as quickly as possible.'
questions.explanation_ar: proceed with تعني المضي قدمًا في تنفيذ شيء.
questions.explanation_en: Proceed with means to continue or start doing something planned.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
choices: Could I lend your phone, please?
Could you borrow me your phone?
Could I borrow your phone, please?
questions.explanation_ar: borrow = أن تأخذ. نقول Could I borrow your phone?
questions.explanation_en: Borrow = take. We say 'Could I borrow your phone?'

questions.question: Anna's phone doesn't work because…
questions.explanation_en: Anna says her battery has run out.

questions.question: Which sentence uses the present perfect to give news?
questions.explanation_ar: I've closed يتكوّن من have + التصريف الثالث: مضارع تام.
questions.explanation_en: 'I've closed' is have + past participle: present perfect.

questions.question: What does 'predicament' mean?
questions.explanation_ar: predicament تعني مأزقًا أو موقفًا صعبًا.
questions.explanation_en: A predicament is a difficult situation.

questions.question: 'I've lost the signal' means…
choices: my phone is not connected any more
questions.explanation_ar: lose the signal تعني انقطاع شبكة الهاتف.
questions.explanation_en: It means the phone has no connection.

questions.question: Which is the most polite way to ask for help?
choices: I wonder if Tom could help me.
questions.explanation_ar: I wonder if… أسلوب مهذب وغير مباشر للطلب.
questions.explanation_en: 'I wonder if…' is a soft, polite way to ask.
